epistemic_status: PROSPECTIVE MEASUREMENT. Characterises when books suspend and how they reopen around information events. A gap in our own capture is not a suspension; the two must be distinguished by evidence, not assumption.

contradictions_found.description: This node's spawn instructions (orchestrator system message) direct: write ONLY SUSPENSION.json + REPORT_BODY.md, and explicitly 'Do NOT write REPORT.md'. The node's own generated contract (experiments/player_program/orchestration/prompts/M17_SUSPENSION_REOPENING.md, 'Required outputs' section) instead names REPORT.md + FINDINGS.json, and its 'Validation that will be run against your output' step is literally `json.load(open('.../M17_SUSPENSION_REOPENING/FINDINGS.json'))`. The M03_CAPTURE_UPGRADE node hit the identical conflict (CAPTURE_REPORT.md placeholder in that directory records the harness refusing a literal REPORT.md write) and resolved it the same way: content prepared in full, delivered under the alternate filename the spawn instructions actually permit, coordinator to copy at integration. Not silently reconciled: both filename pairs are produced here (REPORT_BODY.md per the direct instruction; SUSPENSION.json AND a duplicate FINDINGS.json with identical content so the contract's own json.load validation step can still pass).
contradictions_found.resolution: Wrote REPORT_BODY.md (not REPORT.md) per direct orchestrator instruction. Wrote SUSPENSION.json as the primary structured output per the orchestrator instruction, and additionally wrote FINDINGS.json (byte-identical content) solely so the contract's stated validation command does not fail. Flagging for the coordinator rather than guessing which document controls.

market_status_write_path_audit.finding: flatten_odds_payload() (game markets, line 152) writes market_status='active' if outcomes else 'missing' -- keyed per (book, market) that DOES appear in the vendor payload; a book/market entirely absent from the payload produces no row at all (neither active nor missing). flatten_props_payload() (props, lines 202/222) writes 'active' whenever any outcome exists, and 'missing' only as a single EVENT-level placeholder row when the entire event returns zero outcomes across every book and market. No code path in this writer ever emits market_status='suspended', despite it being a legal value in MARKET_STATUS_VALUES. The vendor's /odds and /events/{id}/odds endpoints do not expose a book-suspended flag distinct from 'no outcomes in this payload' -- so even if The Odds API's upstream book suspended a market, this writer could only ever record that as 'missing' (event-level, props only) or as a silent absence of a row (game markets), never as a labeled suspension.

cadence_gap_seconds_between_written_cycl.note: This is the gap between cycles that produced a NEW/CHANGED markets.jsonl row, not the gap between HTTP polls -- see poll_log below for true poll cadence.

best_line_jsonl.caveat: n_active_orders==0 is a thin-liquidity / no-resting-orders observation on ONE side of ONE market, derived from /orders. It is NOT a market-suspension signal: at every one of these 511 rows, the corresponding markets.jsonl entry for that marketHash (when present) still reads status=ACTIVE. Zero-liquidity and book-suspended are different, unconflated phenomena in this data.

poll_log_jsonl.markets_active_n_returned_series_note: n_returned for /markets/active fell from 90-100 (first ~35 min of capture) to a 28-44 plateau for the remaining ~10.5 hours. This is fully explained by normal game-lifecycle turnover: gameTime values on the earliest-dropping markets are 2026-08-07T01:00-02:00, i.e. already at or past tip-off when this capture window opened at 02:39. No HTTP failure coincides with the drop (0/767 failures across the whole run), which rules out poll failure as the cause. No isolated mid-window dip-then-recovery pattern tied to a single still-scheduled game was observed in the aggregate count; a per-market roster reconstruction (see structural finding below) would be needed to rule that out at the individual-market level, and the current artifacts do not support that reconstruction.

status_transitions.finding: Zero market_status / status transitions of any kind were observed in either tape across the full captured window (odds-API ladder: ~6h50m, 4 games, 3152 rows; sxbet exchange: ~10h51m and still running at measurement time, 9 games, 314 markets.jsonl rows / 6333 orderbook rows / 4449 best_line rows / 7442 trades). This is a preserved negative result, not an absence of measurement.

duration_measurements_note: Not applicable -- zero transitions observed to bound. No suspension interval exists in the data to measure a lower or upper bound on.
price_jump_measurements_note: Not applicable -- reopening price-jump measurement (acceptance criterion 3) requires a reopening event; none occurred in the captured window. Nothing was computed here that could be mistaken for a measured effect.

structural_findings.finding: market_snapshot_schema.py defines market_status in {'active', 'suspended', 'missing'}, but market_snapshot_writer.py (the only writer of snapshots.csv) contains no code path that ever assigns 'suspended' -- verified by reading flatten_odds_payload() (line 152) and flatten_props_payload() (lines 202, 222) in full. Even if the underlying sportsbook suspended a market mid-poll, The Odds API's response shape (an event/bookmaker/market/outcomes payload with no book-suspended flag) gives this writer nothing to key 'suspended' off of. The schema enum's 'suspended' value is currently unreachable in practice.

capture_sxbet.py's SxBetClient.get_active_markets() calls /markets/active exclusively (line 221-227). By the endpoint's own contract, it returns only markets the exchange currently considers active; a suspended market does not appear in the response with a non-ACTIVE status -- it simply does not appear. This is corroborated by the empirical census: 314/314 markets.jsonl rows across the whole run read status='ACTIVE', and the same is true of orderbook.jsonl's orderStatus (6333/6333 ACTIVE), which is drawn from /orders, another endpoint that appears to return only currently-open orders.

structural_findings.severity: material to feasibility -- the central finding of this node
structural_findings.finding: build_envelope() in capture_sxbet.py (lines 390-426) writes a new markets.jsonl row only when a marketHash's content is NEW or has CHANGED (byte-hash comparison against StateStore); byte-identical content is deduplicated and produces no row. No per-cycle roster snapshot (the full list of marketHashes /markets/active returned on a given cycle) is persisted anywhere -- poll_log.jsonl records only the COUNT (n_returned), not the membership. Consequence: if a market were suspended (vanishes from /markets/active for one or more cycles) and then reopened with IDENTICAL content to before, this writer would record nothing at all -- no removal event, no reappearance event, no gap. A suspend/reopen cycle with unchanged content is invisible to the persisted data by construction. This means the acceptance criterion 'a suspension is claimed only from capture evidence that distinguishes book-suspended from we-failed-to-poll' currently has no capture evidence to claim from in either direction -- not because the evidence says 'no suspensions happened', but because the writer cannot represent a suspension as a positive event even when it has no reason to doubt one occurred. This is distinct from a we-failed-to-poll gap: poll_log.jsonl shows 0/767 HTTP failures, so failed polling is ruled out as an explanation for anything observed or unobserved here -- the gap is in what gets WRITTEN on a successful poll of unchanged content, not in polling itself.

The aggregate n_returned series for /markets/active (poll_log.jsonl) drops from ~90-100 to a 28-44 plateau within the first ~35 minutes of capture. Cross-referencing markets.jsonl content.gameTime shows the earliest-vanishing markets belong to games whose scheduled tip-off (gameTime) was already at or before the capture window's start (e.g. Portland Fire @ Toronto Tempo, gameTime 2026-08-07T02:00:00, capture starting 02:39:05). This is consistent with ordinary in-play/post-game market retirement, not suspension. No claim beyond this consistency check is made -- the data does not support ruling out an intra-game suspension riding on top of this trend for a market that was NOT about to retire, per S3 above.

feasibility_verdict.verdict: NOT YET -- MARKET_MECHANISM_SUPPORTED (M00 Section 3, rung 1) for the PURE_MICROSTRUCTURE class (M00 Section 1.6, suspension/reopening) cannot be reached on the current tape or the current writer design.
reasons: Zero status transitions observed in either tape over the full captured window (odds-API ladder ~6h50m/4 games; sxbet exchange ~10h51m/9 games).
The odds-API ladder writer has no code path to ever emit 'suspended' (S1).

The sxbet writer's dedup-on-unchanged-content design cannot witness a suspend/reopen cycle that leaves content unchanged on reopening (S3) -- this is a capture-architecture gap, not (only) a low base-rate problem.
what_would_change_the_verdict: A capture-upgrade change to the sxbet writer (or a companion process) that persists a per-cycle roster snapshot -- e.g. a heartbeat row per still-tracked marketHash even when content is unchanged, or an explicit 'not present in this cycle's active list' row -- so that absence becomes a witnessed, timestamped event rather than a silent non-write. This is a design change, not a data-accumulation problem, and is a prerequisite for ANY future transition in this tape to be usable as evidence.

For the odds-API ladder: either a vendor-side signal for book-level suspension (not currently exposed by the endpoints this writer calls) or accepting that this tape can only ever support the coarser 'missing' (props, event-level) label -- which still needs to actually occur (0 times so far) and needs per-book/per-market granularity it does not currently have for game markets.

Accumulation of enough live-game capture time, AFTER the above fix, for genuine suspension events (injury review, technical/scoring dispute, replay review, book risk-management pull) to occur and be captured. No base rate for these events at this venue/vendor pair exists in this dataset (n=0 observed in ~17.5 combined tape-hours across 13 total games), so no calendar estimate for 'enough' can be computed -- stating a number here would be an unmeasured guess, which the mandate prohibits.
feasibility_verdict.minimum_sample_for_credible_claims: Per the M00 evidence ladder (Section 3, rung 1) and Section D preregistration discipline this program inherits, a credible F6 (suspension/reopening) endpoint needs a preregistered minimum n of TRUSTED transitions set BEFORE the registration window opens, with UNDERPOWERED as the honest verdict below that n. This node does not set that n itself (that is Section D.2 preregistration territory, owned by the family's registration node, not this audit) -- but notes that n=0 currently, so any endpoint registered today would open UNDERPOWERED by definition and stay there until real transitions accumulate under the fixed writer design above.

could_not_establish: Whether any suspend/reopen event occurred during the captured window that the current writer design simply failed to represent (S3) -- this is unknowable from the persisted artifacts, by construction, not merely unmeasured.
Any duration bound (lower or upper) for a suspension -- none was observed to bound.
Any reopening price-jump measurement -- no reopening event exists in the data.

A base rate or expected-time-to-first-transition for either tape -- would require either historical vendor documentation of suspension frequency (not sourced here) or a much longer observed run; zero transitions in the observed window is not enough to fit a rate.

Whether the sxbet /orders and /markets/active endpoints structurally exclude non-active objects (assumed from the empirical 100% ACTIVE census plus the endpoint names) versus some other explanation for the census -- vendor API documentation was not fetched as part of this audit (would require a live network call outside this node's read-only local-artifact scope); this is stated as the best-supported inference from the endpoint name, the code, and the census, not a vendor-confirmed fact.
